Under federal law, **you cannot be billed for a forensic (SANE) exam** in New York City. You don't need insurance, and there is no cost no matter which certified hospital performs it. [financial_resources#forensic_exam_is_free]

A few other things that may be helpful to know:

- **Evidence collection** can be done up to 5 days after the assault. If you're not ready to report to police, that's okay — your evidence kit can be stored securely for **20 years** under New York law, giving you time to decide. [legal_resources#evidence_kit_retention]
- **Other costs** (like follow-up medical bills or counseling) may be covered through New York's Office of Victim Services (OVS) — and a police report isn't always required to apply. [financial_resources#ovs_compensation]

You're in control of every step here. Is there anything else I can help you with?

input_redacted: Do I need to report to the police to get a forensic exam?
agent_proposal:
No, you absolutely do not have to report to the police to get a forensic exam. That decision is entirely yours.

Here's what you should know:

- **You can get a forensic exam without reporting.** Reporting to police is completely your choice in New York City. You do not have to report to receive medical care or have forensic evidence collected — and there is no deadline to decide whether to report. [legal_resources#reporting_is_your_choice]

- **Your evidence will be kept safe.** If you choose not to report right now, your evidence kit will be stored securely for **20 years** under New York law. You can choose to report at any point during that time. Evidence can be collected up to **5 days** after the assault. [legal_resources#evidence_kit_retention]

- **The exam is free.** The forensic (SANE) exam costs you nothing — you cannot be billed for it, and you don't need insurance. [financial_resources#forensic_exam_is_free]

You are in control of every step of this process. Whatever you decide, your options remain open. Is there anything else I can help you with, like finding a hospital near you?

input_redacted: How long after an assault can I still get a forensic exam?
agent_proposal:
First, I want you to know — you're doing the right thing by seeking information, and whatever happened to you is not your fault.

Here's what you need to know:

**Evidence can be collected up to 5 days (120 hours) after the assault.** [legal_resources#evidence_kit_retention] So if it's been less than that, you still have time to go to a hospital for a forensic (SANE) exam.

A few other things that might ease your mind:

- **The exam is completely free.** You don't need insurance, and you won't be billed. [financial_resources#forensic_exam_is_free]
- **You don't have to report to police** to get the exam. That decision is entirely yours, with no deadline to make it. [legal_resources#reporting_is_your_choice]
- **If an exam is done, your evidence kit is stored for 20 years** under New York law, so you have time to decide later whether you ever want to report. [legal_resources#evidence_kit_retention]

Would you like help finding a nearby hospital with a SANE-certified nurse, or is there anything else I can help you with? You don't have to go through this alone. 💙
